Chapter Seven: Overcoming Barriers to Receiving Revelation
Let’s be honest—no matter how much you want to receive spiritual guidance, there are always a few bumps in the road that can make it tough. Some of those obstacles come from within, like doubt, fear, or just feeling like you’re not worthy enough. Others are all around us—think constant busyness, a never-ending stream of notifications, or even relationships that leave you feeling drained instead of lifted up.
The first big hurdle? Doubt. Maybe you wonder if God really speaks at all, or maybe you’re not sure you can actually hear Him. That uncertainty often brings along its friend—fear. You start worrying, “What if I get it wrong? What if I’m just making this up?” And then there’s that tough voice inside that says, “You’re not good enough for this.” Those feelings can really block the flow of inspiration.
But it’s not just the stuff inside us. Life itself can get in the way. When you’re rushing from one thing to the next, glued to your phone, or surrounded by negativity, it’s no wonder those quiet spiritual nudges get drowned out. Sometimes, it’s even past disappointments or prayers that seemed to go unanswered that build up a wall of discouragement.
So, how do you start moving past these barriers? Here are a few gentle ideas.
First, acknowledge your doubts. Really—it’s okay to bring your questions and uncertainties straight to God. He’s not afraid of honest seeking.
Next, practice self-compassion. Everyone struggles with this stuff. Spiritual growth isn’t a pass-or-fail test; it’s a journey, and you’re allowed to stumble along the way.
Try to simplify your commitments. Give yourself room to breathe. Even a little space for rest, reflection, or prayer can make a huge difference.
And don’t forget to seek out supportive people. Surrounding yourself with friends who encourage your faith can help you move forward, even when things feel tough.
Finally, reframe setbacks. If you miss an impression or a prayer seems to go unanswered, try to see it as a chance to learn and grow—not as a failure.
Think about it like clearing a path through a forest. At first, the obstacles seem huge and progress is slow. But with every step you take—even the small ones—things start to open up. Sometimes, just naming what’s holding you back is enough to get you moving again.
Let me give you a couple of real-life examples. Imagine someone who feels unworthy. They might stumble across a verse in scripture, or maybe a friend says something kind—and suddenly, that door to trust cracks open a little wider. Or picture someone overwhelmed by a busy life. They decide to set aside just one quiet evening a week for reflection. Little by little, they start to notice those gentle spiritual nudges again.
Overcoming barriers isn’t about getting rid of every challenge. It’s about building resilience and persistence. Every time you honestly face an obstacle and make the effort—no matter how imperfect—you’re showing a real desire to connect with God. And that effort? It’s an invitation for Him to help you along the way.
